Need avoid `not(match(E))` dominating. Use only nonmatch atoms in positive/negative combinations that don't accept all. E.g. complex rules:
`(startswith(A,B) and contains(C,D)) allow;`
`(endswith(D,A) or match(E)) allow;`
`(contains(C,D) and startswith(A,B)) drop;`
`not(endswith(D,A))` alone dominates all sequences not ending D,A, nearly all; avoid top-level not unless combined AND with something.
Use expressions:

3 `(contains(C,D) and startswith(A,B)) drop;`
4 `(startswith(A,B) and (contains(C,D) or endswith(D,A))) allow;`
5 `(endswith(D,A) and contains(C,D)) allow;`

import random,time
from syntax import parse_policy
from ebpf.create_dfa import create,PolicyError

base='(startswith(A,B) and contains(C,D)) allow;(endswith(D,A) or match(E)) allow;(contains(C,D) and startswith(A,B)) drop;(startswith(A,B) and (contains(C,D) or endswith(D,A))) allow;(endswith(D,A) and contains(C,D)) allow;'
